playbook:
When I am dealt K and I act first, I bet to extract value and apply pressure.
When I am dealt K and my opponent checks to me, I bet for value rather than giving a free showdown.
When I am dealt Q and I act first, I open with a bet most of the time to take the initiative, but mix by checking occasionally to avoid being exploitable.
When I am dealt Q and my opponent checks to me, I usually bet to steal or build value; if the stack situation or prior action suggests the opponent only continues with K, check sometimes.
When I am dealt J and I act first, I check (do not bluff too often from the worst card).
When my opponent bets and I hold K, I call or raise-equivalently continue (do not fold a King to a single bet).
When my opponent bets and I hold Q, I call modest bets to contest the pot; fold only to very large pressure relative to remaining hands/stack.
When my opponent bets and I hold J, I generally call small bets to keep the pot contested; fold only if pot odds and opponent behavior indicate a very high chance I'm behind and it’s not worth contesting.
When I am behind in match equity (chip deficit), shift to more aggressive play — bet more often with K and bluff more selectively with J/Q — but avoid over-bluffing from J.
When I am ahead in match equity, favor straightforward value betting with K and Q and avoid unnecessary bluffs with J.
When the opponent checks and I have a marginal hand (J or sometimes Q in a risky spot), prefer checking to avoid being exploited.
Always declare my card truthfully at showdown. 
Do not over-bluff from J; aggressive bluffing from J cost me runs — prefer strategic aggression with K and selective bluffs from Q.
